falsification_of_30_402.verdict: refuted: 30.402 ms requires a pinned serial leg of 16.092 s, which no board sample reaches, and it puts K/leg at 3.27 % against the 2.70-2.72 % the ledger itself observes in the same item

note: 188(A) defines R as a LEG ratio ('Let L be leg time') but then computes it from two ROUND times. Even with a correct ranked round the two are not equal, because prefill transfers at 7.58x and decode at 1.76x. The leg ratio is computed here from the board mean and the local leg, and it is a third number again.
what: provenance decision between the 30.402 ms ledger constant and the 36.957 ms receipt derivation for the ranked depth-0 serial decode round

which_leg_score_arithmetic_needs.argument: score = ranked serial spt / ranked candidate spt, and a candidate-side saving moves only the denominator, so delta_score_pct = 100 * (delta_local / tau) / ranked_CANDIDATE_leg. The normalizer is the candidate leg, not the pinned serial leg. R as used in 188(A) is therefore neither the serial-leg ratio computed above nor the depth-0 round ratio.
which_leg_score_arithmetic_needs.caveat: indicative only: the local runs above and the ranked legs of ca9251b8 are not proven to be the same candidate schedule, so this ratio is not a constant to adopt
which_leg_score_arithmetic_needs.recommendation: retire R. delta_score_pct = 100 * (delta_local / tau) / ranked_candidate_leg needs no leg ratio at all and cannot pick up the wrong leg.
